name: manual_362926
claim: In Python, sqlite3.Connection as a context manager commits on success and rolls back on exception but does not close. To close without changing transaction semantics, wrap the transaction manager inside contextlib.closing (with closing(connection) as conn: with conn: ...), or use a close-always helper that commits or rolls back before closing; run new tests with ResourceWarning treated as an error.

decisions.notes: PR #450 review correction: preserve sqlite3 transaction semantics by making contextlib.closing the outer context or by using a close-always helper; the original candidate remains historical and this accepted lesson supersedes it.
